Theme portrait · research pilot [scope-97]

Portrait: cyberpunk

What makes Cyberpunk Cyberpunk, drawn on the package's real stylesheets and components and fixed to this theme. Every word, role and verb comes from themes/cyberpunk/signature.json, and every claim there cites the token, selector or keyframes that proves it; tests/theme-portraits.spec.mjs refuses a citation the stylesheet does not contain. Each of the nine sections is a block with its own verdict. A row or verb marked Open is a proposal for Kenny, not a fact about the theme.

1 · Idea

Look at: the idea is at most three sentences, and the list under it is what may not move. Read each claim against the rest of this page: every later section should be explainable from these lines, and a claim that nothing below shows is a claim to strike. Each claim carries its proof, the token, selector or keyframes in cyberpunk's own files that make it true.

Signal yellow on a void with a violet cast: yellow acts and grounds, blood red alarms, cyan labels what must be read. Every corner is square or cut by a notch, the type is uppercase and spaced, and machine prefixes (///, >, !!) speak for the interface. Motion is a signal being acquired: text deciphers out of noise, a slice burst fires once, a charge sweeps across a button.

  1. Yellow acts and grounds, red alarms, cyan labels: swap any two and it is a different theme.

    Proof
    • themes/cyberpunk/tokens.json --primary
    • themes/cyberpunk/tokens.json --destructive
    • themes/cyberpunk/tokens.json --accent

  2. The app ink is a warm smoke on a violet-cast void, never white on black.

    Proof

  3. The radius is 0: every corner is square or a notch cut off it.

  4. Headings, buttons, links and labels are uppercase and letter-spaced; labels and identifiers speak in the mono face.

2 · Colour in its role

Look at: 9 roles, each a swatch of its token as the page resolves it, what the role may carry, what it may never carry, and a live component using it. The swatch and the component must show the same colour. Then read across the cards: a colour that appears in a component under a role it is told never to take is a finding. Roles in cyberpunk: Signal, Void, Smoke, Label, Alarm, Red on yellow, Boundary, Hairline, Glitch violet.

Signal

--primary

Use
The primary action's fill, the navbar and hero ground, the section heading's brackets, the selected tab's underline, the focus ring.
Never
Body text in long runs, or a large ground inside the app surface; it is the one colour that is both a surface and a signal, so it is spent on those two jobs only.

4 · Shape

Look at: the corners, the edges and what floats. Radius, borders, shadows, and last the one shape this theme is recognised by. Every example is the component as it ships; check that its corner, edge and shadow are the ones the sentence above it describes, at this zoom and at 200 %.

Radius

0 everywhere: the token is 0 and the register restates border-radius: 0 on badges, cards, panels, tabs and pickers.

PlainDraftOfferRejected
Saved. The handover note is visible to the day shift.
Proof
  • themes/cyberpunk/tokens.json --radius
  • css/cyberpunk-register.css [data-theme='cyberpunk'] .kp-popover

Borders

A button has no border: its frame is the background colour, the face is inset 2px and a 10px slit runs through the middle. Cards and panels take a 1px hairline; toasts and alerts a 3px left edge.

Proof
  • css/cyberpunk-register.css --kp-button-slit
  • css/cyberpunk-register.css [data-theme='cyberpunk'] .kp-toast
  • css/cyberpunk-register.css [data-theme='cyberpunk'] .kp-alert

Shadows

None. Buttons and cards set box-shadow: none; the focus ring is an inset box-shadow drawn on the face, inside the clip.

Signature

The notch. A button's bottom-right corner is cut by 14px, an input, badge, toast and alert by 8px; a card cuts its top-right by 16px; a dialog and the spec sheet cut two opposite corners by 18px; a button pointing back carries the notch bottom-left.

5 · Surfaces

Look at: each ground with the same card and the same two buttons on it. On every ground the card must read as raised in this theme's own way, the primary button must be the loudest thing, and no text may sink into its ground. 6 · Motion

Look at: first the live copies above the stage. Each verb has a Replay button that plays the register's own rule on a real component: hover and press are the register's :hover and :active rules applied by the page, not a copy of them. Then switch Reduced motion on and replay each again: what is left must be exactly the column "Reduced motion" in the table. Flicker in cyberpunk: allowed, Glitch is this theme's own vocabulary: the headline's slice burst and the nav link's hover slice already step between frames, each with its rate in reports/di5.md. Every verb has an answer.
For every copy below

Follows your system setting until you press it; the page rewrites its own motion guards, so the stylesheets decide what remains.

8 · Voice

Look at: how cyberpunk talks: its case, the small words and prefixes it puts in front of things, how it draws instead of using icons, and what it never does. The sample under the list is real markup; every rule in the list should be visible in it.
Case
UPPERCASE for headings, buttons, nav links, labels, badges, tabs and the breadcrumb; running text as written.
Labels
  • A microlabel starts with '/// '.
  • A field label starts with '> ' and is mono cyan.
  • An error starts with '!! '.
  • Breadcrumb steps are joined by '//'; menu items start with '— '.
  • A stamp carries the consumer's own label (js/strings.js), never a word written in CSS.
Icons
Drawn geometry instead of icons: a health dot is a square turned 45deg, a dropdown link carries a CSS caret, the checkbox tick is a notched block.
Never
  • Pure black, or white text on the void.
  • Violet outside a glitch slice.
  • A rounded corner or a soft shadow.
  • A second loop besides the data stream and the marquee.

Worked example: a banner that asks for attention

A banner that asks for attention, from existing parts only: an app surface with a microlabel, the destructive alert (notched, 3px left edge, the words 'Warning:' carrying the meaning), the primary and ghost buttons, and the data stream closing it off. Nothing here is new CSS.

Parts used: .kp-alert .kp-alert--destructive .kp-alert__body .kp-alert__icon .kp-alert__label .kp-button .kp-button--ghost .kp-button--primary .kp-row .kp-section .kp-stack .microlabel; hooks data-kp-divider data-kp-semantic data-kp-surface.
